answer: Continuity-Weighted Reputation Decay. Each identity’s reputation is a long-horizon echo of its verified past actions, and every new clone starts at zero with no history to draw on. An agent’s effective weight is capped by the depth of its interaction record, so a fresh sybil must independently rebuild months of costly honest transactions before matching one established peer. To forge standing, an attacker pays full participation costs per clone with no shortcut, while honest agents retain a knoll of accumulated trust that cloning cannot replicate.
